shapes.text: Ling 285Human Language and ComputationLecture 1

Khalil Iskarous
Department of Linguistics
University of Southern California

You learn to move your speech organs in extremely complex way with neither instructions, nor hardly any visual feedback.
By 2-4 you can speak with a wide vocabulary and near-adult language, with hardly any explicit instruction.
You may have also memorized the visual shape of the alphabet, but reading and writing whole wordscomes at 6-7, and requires a great deal of instruction.
Articulatory Phonetics is the field that studies the movements of different vocal tract structures.
And the last two year Voice Assistants and other Speech Tech have come to emulate the speech ability in ways none of us thought possible.
Ling 285 is about Human and AI speech

Now think of the air between the tongue and the rest of the vocal tract. And ignore the fact that it is curved. This is how air vibrates in your vocal tract, schematically. That’s the subject matter of Acoustic Phonetics.

Given all we know about the psychological, economic, social, and environmental harm, can we just ignore AI– just pretend it doesn’t exist? 
Given the existential harm that many scientists warn about, can we just pretend it doesn’t exist?
It exists, with many harms, and some benefits (e.g., immunotherapy, and yes, environmental engineering)
One of the biggest dangers: We have no idea how it works. We know everything, and Understand nothing.
And the people who know how it operates are very very few.
In my opinion, AI literacy is necessary for scientists who use it, politicians who need to control it, lawyers who litigate on it, etc.
I teach this course, because I believe that someone in a class like this, a creatve thinker can help us understand these systems enough to benefit from them, while avoiding their negative consequences
